newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Paris stocks hit record, rest of Europe dull.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Paris stocks hit record, rest of Europe dull.

text.p: Paris stocks soared to an all-time high on Wednesday, boosted by new opinion polls showing a big win for the centre-right government in upcoming elections, but the rest of Europe made a mixed showing.
In currencies, the dollar gained a pfennig after supportive comments from a Bundesbank council member and rekindled speculation that the U.S. central bank may increase interest rates next week.

London and Frankfurt trade was lacklustre after hitting record levels on Tuesday but French shares climbed to an intra-day record of 2,765.91 points on the CAC 40 index and eclipsing the previous all-time high of 2,736.71 set two months ago.
Paris investors were encouraged by the stronger dollar which improved export prospects and the poll lead for the government parties, regarded as more sympathetic to business.
"All signs are on green, the dollar, the bond market and the polls," a broker said.

A CSA poll on Tuesday night gave 317 seats to the centre-right majority against 215 to the Socialists and allies. This followed a BVA poll giving 303 to the majority and 226 to the Socialists and allies.
Jacques Chahine Finance has predicted that if the government parties win, fund managers saw the CAC heading above 3,000. If the Socialists win it could fall to 2,400.
But dealers said some factors could puncture the French euphoria.

Large fund inflows were currently fuelling the market as foreign funds take comfort from the polls and invest in France, which has been lagging behind other markets. But a poll showing a swing back to the Socialists could scare these investors away again.
In London, Europe's biggest bourse, stocks drifted lower
after a record-breaking run which has seen the blue-chip FTSE 100 index climb 10 percent in the last four weeks.
By midday, shares had slipped into the negative column after making healthy gains in early trade. But dealers said some consolidation was inevitable after the recent bull run.
"We won't see much selling pressure today. Very few people want to sell stock at the moment," one senior dealer said. "But market makers will mark down prices until the buyers step in again."
In Frankfurt, trading on the computerised IBIS index
climbed 0.6 percent in early dealings but floor trade, which closed at a peak on Tuesday, fell 0.4 percent by midday.
Deutsche Telekom was a one of the main losers, following reports that Bonn might consider selling some its Telekom shares to help cut its budget deficit.
On currency markets, the dollar was stronger after
comments from a Bundesbank council member.

Ernst Welteke said in Vienna: "It seems that a dollar rate at around 1.70 marks conforms with the real data." His Bundesbank colleague Klaus-Dieter Kuebacher said later in Warsaw he also believed dollar/mark levels were good.
"Welteke is certainly giving the impression the weakness of the mark is not a problem at these levels," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.

Sources close to the Federal Reserve central bank told Reuters that there was a good chance of a 25 basis point rise in the 5.50 percent Federal funds target rate when the policy-making Federal Open Market
Elsewhere, sterling rallied in early trading against a generally weaker mark . It was at 2.7822 marks compared to 2.7687 in late trade yesterday.

The pound was stronger on Tuesday affter the Bank of England said the recent strength of sterling improved the inflation outlook this year but that another interest rate rise was likely to be necessary to keep a lid on prices.
STOCK PRICES AT 1100 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was down 18.5 points at 4,672.5.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 44.56 points at 2,764.08.
Frankfurt's DAX index was down 21.46 points at 3,573.69.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7067 marks compared with 1.6965 late in Europe on Tuesday and 118.82 yen versus 118.83.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $349.00 an ounce after closing at $348.05 in London on Tuesday. Silver was up one cent at $4.86.
